title: Fronting in the Story of the Vaquero

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *Crucial fue la intervención del mediador* and *En aquella ciudad comenzó la rebelión* from B2 Unit 1: this is fronting. You put the piece you want to stress at the front of the sentence, and the subject usually comes after the verb. Writers use it to give a paragraph a high point. This lesson applies it to the life of the vaqueros and to the carne asada.

sections.title: What can go first
rows: Duros eran los días de trabajo. (Hard were the days of work.)
Place or time phrase + verb + subject
En estas tierras nació la cultura vaquera. (In these lands vaquero culture was born.)
Típicos del norte son los asados en familia. (Typical of the north are family barbecues.)

sections.title: Two rules to keep
sections.content: The verb and the adjective agree with the subject that comes after them: *Duro era el trabajo*, *Duros eran los días*, not *Duros era los días*. The subject stays behind the verb: *Duro el trabajo era* sounds unnatural. Plain order is still the usual order; fronting is for the moment you want to stress.

items.spanish: Duros eran los días de trabajo en los agostaderos.
items.english: Hard were the days of work on the grazing lands.

items.spanish: Con el lazo en la mano arreaba el vaquero el ganado.
items.english: With the lasso in his hand the vaquero herded the cattle.

items.spanish: En estas tierras nació la cultura vaquera.
items.english: In these lands vaquero culture was born.

items.spanish: Muy larga era la jornada, que empezaba antes de salir el sol.
items.english: Very long was the working day, which began before sunrise.

items.spanish: Típica del norte es la carne asada con la familia.
items.english: Typical of the north is the carne asada with the family.

sections.content: Use fronting once in a paragraph, at the point you want to stress. If every sentence starts with its adjective, the text sounds heavy.
